blocks.md:
- **Swapping precision and recall.** Precision divides by everything **predicted** positive; recall by everything **actually** positive.
- **Trusting accuracy with rare classes.** Always-0 can score 90%+.
- **Mixing up FP and FN.** The second letter is the **prediction** (P = predicted positive).

blocks.title: Metrics from a confusion matrix
blocks.problem: A failure model on 200 machines: TP = 12, FN = 8, FP = 6, TN = 174. Compute all four metrics.

steps.md:
```python
TP, FN, FP, TN = 12, 8, 6, 174
accuracy = (TP + TN) / (TP + FN + FP + TN)
precision = TP / (TP + FP)
recall = TP / (TP + FN)
f1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
print(round(accuracy, 3), round(precision, 3), round(recall, 3), round(f1, 3))
```

```text
0.93 0.667 0.6 0.632
```

blocks.title: Solution: Score the failure model
blocks.md:
Full program for **Score the failure model** (try it yourself first):

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("failures.csv")
a, p = df["Actual"], df["Predicted"]

TP = np.count_nonzero((a == 1) & (p == 1))
TN = np.count_nonzero((a == 0) & (p == 0))
FP = np.count_nonzero((a == 0) & (p == 1))
FN = np.count_nonzero((a == 1) & (p == 0))

accuracy = (TP + TN) / len(df)
precision = TP / (TP + FP)
recall = TP / (TP + FN)
f1 = 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
print("TP", TP, "TN", TN, "FP", FP, "FN", FN)
print("accuracy", round(accuracy, 3))
print("precision", round(precision, 3))
print("recall", round(recall, 3))
print("F1", round(f1, 3))
```

Output:

```text
TP 21 TN 364 FP 7 FN 8
accuracy 0.962
precision 0.75
recall 0.724
F1 0.737
```
